card.title: Front-desk POS
card.sub: Sale, payment and a QR to the customer's phone in seconds. The highest-volume channel, digitised.

hero.h1: The POS that digitises your front desk: sale, contract and payment in seconds
hero.lede: Between 70% and 85% of a jet ski operator's revenue comes through the front desk. It is also the channel still running on folders, photocopies and ballpoint signatures. A POS built for watersports rental turns it into a flow of seconds that the customer finishes on their own phone.

bullets: Load the sale in seconds: product, time slot, number of craft and extras
Card or cash payment taken on the spot, on the same screen
QR code to the customer's phone so they handle their details, ID and signature
Staff mode and self-service kiosk mode on the same device

sections.h: Why a generic POS doesn't work at a rental desk

blocks.text: A hospitality POS knows how to take payment, but it does not know you are renting out an asset that has to come back. It knows nothing about time slots, fleet availability, craft registration, the contract that has to be signed or the official register that has to be filled in afterwards. You end up with the POS for payment and a folder next to it for everything else.

The August result is familiar: two to three staff hours a day transcribing details and chasing signatures, exactly in the busiest slots, and a queue on the dock that is revenue walking over to the operator next door.

sections.h: How a front-desk sale works, step by step

items: Staff load the sale: product, time slot, number of craft and extras. Availability is the same one the website and WhatsApp use, so the same craft can never be sold twice.
Payment is taken on the spot, by card or cash, without leaving the sales screen.
The system generates a QR code tied to that booking. The customer scans it with their phone and carries on alone, freeing up the desk.
While the customer fills in their details and signs, staff are already serving the next person.

blocks.text: The same device works two ways depending on the time of day. In staff mode your team drives it, optimised for dispatching fast at peak. In kiosk mode it faces the customer so simple sales resolve themselves, and staff only step in when needed.

items: Real availability shared with the website, WhatsApp and partners
Pricing by season, duration, base and product applied automatically
Extras and upsells suggested at the point of sale
Cash-up by base and by shift, with no manual count

blocks.text: The front desk stops being an admin station and becomes a point of sale. Staff no longer transcribe details, so that time goes into selling extras, managing fleet rotation and looking after whoever is waiting. For high-volume operators this typically means recovering two to three staff hours a day in peak season.

faq.q: Do I need to buy new hardware?
faq.a: No proprietary terminal is required. It runs on a tablet or a computer with a browser, and works with the card reader you already use or one connected to the payment gateway.

faq.q: Does the customer need to install an app?
faq.a: No. The QR code opens a web page in the customer's mobile browser. No downloads, no sign-up, no account to create.

faq.q: What if the customer has no phone or struggles with it?
faq.a: The same flow can be completed on the tablet at the desk. Staff walk the customer through it and the signature is captured on screen.

faq.q: Does it work if the base loses internet?
faq.a: Boarding and QR scanning work offline and sync once the connection is back. Card payment does need connectivity, as with any POS.

card.title: Digital contracts
card.sub: A valid electronic signature on the customer's phone, with watersports-rental clauses.

hero.h1: Rental contracts with a digital signature: legally sound, on the customer's phone, in 15 seconds
hero.lede: The contract is what covers you when something goes wrong, and it is exactly what gets filled in at speed during high season, signed illegibly and filed in a folder nobody opens again. Digitally it stops being paperwork and becomes one more field on the booking.

bullets: Electronic signature with timestamp and document hash, under the eIDAS framework
Templates written for watersports rental, not adapted from a generic agreement
Contracts for minors signed by the legal guardian and tied to the same booking
Permanent archive, searchable by customer, craft, date or contract number

sections.h: What a watersports rental contract has to cover

blocks.text: The templates cover what the sector actually needs, which is what a generic rental model leaves out: licensed and unlicensed operation, the limits of the authorised navigation area, deposits and security holds, damage to the craft and to third parties, weather conditions, and the specific case of minors, where the legal guardian signs.

items: Identification of the parties and of the craft, with registration
Contracted time slot and return conditions
Deposit, liability for damage and insurance cover
Data-processing and image-use consents
Minors annex with the guardian's details and signature
The booking generates the contract already filled in with what the system knows: customer, product, slot, base and price.
The customer opens it on their phone, from the QR code at the desk or the link on their online booking, and completes what is missing: ID document and personal details.
They sign on screen with a finger. If minors are involved, the annex is added and the guardian signs.
The document is sealed, filed and sent to the customer by email or WhatsApp. The data flows straight into the official register.

blocks.text: The signature is an advanced electronic signature: there is a record of which document was signed, when, from which device and with what cryptographic hash. That is what lets you prove, months later and against a claim, that this specific customer accepted these specific terms.
Contracts stay filed and findable. When a damage claim arrives about something from three months ago, locating the signed contract stops being an excavation through cardboard boxes.

faq.q: Is an electronic signature as valid as a handwritten one?
faq.a: It is an advanced electronic signature with a timestamp and a document hash, under the eIDAS regulation. Against a ballpoint signature it has an evidential advantage: it records when and from where it was signed.

faq.q: Can I use my own contract model?
faq.a: Yes. You can start from the sector templates or upload the contract your company already uses and digitise it with the same automatic fields.

faq.q: How are rentals to minors handled?
faq.a: The contract includes an annex with the minor's details and the legal guardian's signature, tied to the same booking. It is not a loose document filed separately.

faq.q: Just looking for the PDF template?
faq.a: If what you need right now is a model to print, there is a free downloadable template with all the essential clauses in our rental contract guide, linked below.

card.sub: Replies in under 30 s, in any language, and closes the booking with payment and contract.

hero.h1: The WhatsApp agent that answers, charges and signs bookings on its own
hero.lede: Almost every chatbot in the sector can reply. The difference is what happens next: this agent checks your real availability, generates the payment link, takes the money and gets the contract signed inside the same conversation. It doesn't hand you a lead — it closes the sale.

bullets: Replies in under 30 seconds, at any hour, in the customer's language
Checks real fleet availability before proposing a time slot
Takes payment inside the conversation and gets the contract signed, without leaving WhatsApp
Escalates to a human whenever the conversation goes off script

blocks.text: A high-volume operator gets around fifty enquiries a day across WhatsApp, Instagram and website forms. Most arrive outside office hours, at weekends, or exactly when the team is busy on the dock. Any enquiry that takes more than an hour to answer very likely becomes a booking with a competitor.
You do not fix that by hiring someone to reply to messages. You fix it by making the reply instant, accurate and able to take payment.

items: Replies in the customer's language, including German, English, French and Italian
Checks real availability before proposing a time slot
Recommends product and duration based on what the customer asks for, and suggests extras
Clears the recurring questions: licence, minimum age, fuel, deposit, meeting point
Generates the payment link and confirms the booking with no input from your team
Triggers the contract signature so boarding is immediate on arrival

blocks.text: The agent is trained on your real information: your fleet, your bases, your prices, your policies and your tone. It is not a canned-response bot or a menu tree.

sections.h: Chatbot, booking agent, and an agent that closes

blocks.text: Three different things get sold under the same name. A chatbot replies with pre-written text and hands off to a person. A booking agent checks availability and proposes times, but still passes the case to your team to take payment. An agent that closes does both of the above and then charges and gets the contract signed, without anyone on your team touching the conversation.
That last part is what moves the number: as long as payment depends on someone replying, you keep losing the eleven-at-night bookings.

faq.q: Can it get it wrong and sell something I don't have?
faq.a: It does not offer slots that do not exist: it checks real availability before replying. When a request falls outside what is configured, it hands the conversation to a human instead of improvising.

faq.q: Does it take over my current WhatsApp number?
faq.a: The agent works on your business number through the official WhatsApp Business API. Your team still sees every conversation and can step in at any point.

faq.q: Which languages does it reply in?
faq.a: It detects the customer's language and replies in it. In practice the most common ones around the Mediterranean are English, German, French and Italian, alongside Spanish.

faq.q: Can people tell it's an AI?
faq.a: It is trained on your tone and your real information, and answers with concrete details about your fleet and prices. When a conversation gets complicated it hands over to a person rather than improvising.

meta.description: Chase mode spots the checkout that dropped and the enquiry that never closed, and recovers them over WhatsApp with an automatic follow-up that stops the moment the customer pays.
meta.ogTitle: The bookings you're losing in silence

card.title: Lost booking recovery
card.sub: Recovers abandoned checkouts and open enquiries, over WhatsApp and automatically.

hero.h1: The bookings you lose in silence, the system chases and closes
hero.lede: Nobody tells you about the booking that never happened. The customer who reached the payment screen and didn't finish, or the one who asked on a Thursday and never wrote back, appear in no report: they are simply absent. Chase mode finds them and goes after them.

bullets: Spots the checkout that reached payment and was never completed
Spots the enquiry that stayed open and never closed
Automatic follow-up over WhatsApp, the channel where customers actually reply
Stops on its own the moment the customer pays or asks not to be contacted again

sections.h: The revenue that shows up in no report

blocks.text: An operator's reports measure what happened: bookings, revenue, occupancy. What they do not measure is what almost happened. The customer who picked product and slot, reached the payment screen and left because the phone rang; the one who asked on WhatsApp, got an answer and never wrote back. Those two situations are, by volume, the biggest pool of lost revenue for an operator with traffic — and they are invisible.

In e-commerce this problem has had a name and a fix for years: abandoned cart recovery. In watersports rental almost nobody applies it, and there is an added advantage here: the recovery channel is not email, it is WhatsApp.

items: The system logs the attempt: which product, which slot, and exactly where the customer dropped out.
It leaves a sensible margin, so it does not message someone who just went to fetch their card.
It follows up on WhatsApp, picking the conversation back up where it stopped, with the product and slot the customer had already chosen and a payment link ready.
If there is no reply, it makes a second attempt with updated availability. If the customer pays, or asks not to be contacted again, the follow-up stops.

sections.h: Why it works better on WhatsApp than by email

blocks.text: A cart-recovery email competes with fifty other emails and gets opened, at best, the next day. A WhatsApp message lands in the same thread where the customer was already talking to you, gets read within minutes and can be answered in one line. For a booking that also has a date — Saturday afternoon's slot expires — those hours are what decide whether it is recovered.

items: Picks up the existing thread instead of opening a cold conversation
The payment link travels inside the message, without restarting the process
If the original slot is gone, it proposes the closest alternative
Every recovery is attributed in the reporting, so you know what it contributes

faq.q: Isn't it intrusive to message someone who didn't finish paying?
faq.a: Messages go to people who already started a conversation or a purchase with you, in the same thread, with a time margin before the first message. The follow-up stops as soon as the customer pays or asks not to receive more messages.

faq.q: How many messages does it send?
faq.a: Few and spaced out: a first attempt after a sensible margin and, if there is no reply, a second with updated availability. The aim is to recover the sale, not to hound the customer.

faq.q: Does it also recover enquiries that never reached payment?
faq.a: Yes. Beyond the abandoned checkout, it spots conversations left open without a close and picks them up with a concrete proposal.

faq.q: Can I see how much it's recovering?
faq.a: Yes. Every recovered booking is attributed as such in the data dashboard, separate from the other channels.

hero.lede: The partner channel usually runs on calls to the base manager, loose messages and an end-of-month count that never reconciles first time. With their own portal, the hotel books directly against your real availability and the commission works itself out.

sections.h: The channel that costs the most to administer

blocks.text: An established operator ends up with fifteen or twenty partners: hotels, holiday apartments, inbound agencies, guides and commission-based reps. Each with their own percentage, their own way of settling and their own way of notifying you. A hotel concierge calls the base manager, the manager writes the booking in a notebook, and at the end of the month someone tries to reconstruct who brought which customer.

That reconstruction is where the arguments appear and where both sides lose money: bookings the partner claims to have brought that are nowhere on record, and commissions paid twice because nobody remembers whether they were already settled.

items: You set the partner up with their terms: commission, which products they can sell and which bases they can access.
The partner logs in with their own access and sees real availability — the same one the front desk and the website use.
They book directly for their customer. The booking lands in your system already attributed to them, with no calls or middlemen.
The commission is calculated then and there and added to their outstanding balance. Settlement stops being a negotiation.
You: the channel stops depending on someone picking up the phone, and every booking is attributed on the spot
The partner: they see real availability and confirm to their customer immediately, without looking bad waiting on your reply
Both: the outstanding balance is the same number for everyone, viewable at any time

blocks.text: In practice the most visible effect is that partners sell more: when confirming is instant, the concierge offers the activity with more confidence.

faq.q: Can each partner have different terms?
faq.a: Yes. Commission, which products they can sell and which bases they can access are configured per partner.

faq.q: Does the partner see all my prices and occupancy?
faq.a: They see availability and prices for what they are authorised to sell. They do not get access to your internal operations or to the other channels' data.

faq.q: How are commissions settled?
faq.a: The system keeps the outstanding balance current per partner. Settlement happens against that balance, with the detail of the bookings behind it.

faq.q: Does it work for commission-based reps, not just hotels?
faq.a: Yes. The mechanism is the same for hotels, holiday apartments, inbound agencies, guides and your own sales reps.

hero.h1: Your fleet and bases live: who's on the water, which craft is running late, what's happening at each site
hero.lede: Every booking system in the sector finishes its job once the booking is paid. What happens next — who boarded, which craft is on the water, who is twenty minutes late — still lives in the head of whoever runs each base. This is the module that digitises it.

bullets: Real-time dashboard with the status of every base and every craft
QR scanning at boarding, working offline when there is no signal
Automatic alerts when a departure runs late or a return does not arrive
Visibility across every base without being physically at any of them

sections.h: The blind spot of booking software

blocks.text: A multi-base operator knows how much they have sold, but not what is happening right now at the base forty kilometres away. They find out a craft came back late once it has already derailed the next three bookings, and they find out from a phone call, not from the system.
That blindness has a direct cost: dropped slots, customers waiting on the dock, and bad reviews over something that twenty minutes of warning would have solved.

items: The customer arrives with their QR code, either from the contract signed at the desk or from the online booking.
Staff scan it from their phone and the system validates on the spot that payment is done, the contract is signed and the documentation is in order.
The real departure is recorded, with time, assigned craft and fuel level.
On return, the drop-off and any incident are recorded, and the craft is released for the next slot.

blocks.text: Scanning works offline, because coverage on many docks is patchy. Records are stored on the device and sync as soon as the signal is back.

sections.h: Alerts that arrive before the problem does

items: A craft running late on its return, with the minutes accumulated
A departure not registered when the slot has already started
A base with more bookings than available craft in the next hour
An incident logged by staff during the activity

blocks.text: Alerts reach both the base manager and the general manager, so the decision to reshuffle the schedule is taken with room to spare rather than after the fact.

faq.q: Do I need special hardware to scan the QR codes?
faq.a: No. Staff use their own phones. There are no dedicated scanners or terminals to buy.

faq.q: Does it work when there's no coverage on the dock?
faq.a: Yes. Check-in is offline-first: it records boarding on the device and syncs when the connection returns.

faq.q: Can I see several bases at once?
faq.a: Yes. The dashboard shows bases grouped or separately, with each one's fleet status on the same screen.

faq.q: Does it replace the base manager's paper worksheet?
faq.a: That is the point: departures, returns, fuel and incidents are all recorded in the boarding flow, with no parallel notebook.

sections.h: What is the rental contract for?

blocks.text: The jet ski rental contract is the written proof of the conditions the customer accepted: which craft they took, in what condition, for how long, what happens if they damage it and who is liable in an accident. Without it, any incident becomes your word against theirs.
It's not red tape: it's what keeps you from paying for a breakdown, a fine or a claim yourself. In practice, a signed contract prevents 90% of the arguments at the desk when the craft comes back.

sections.h: What a jet ski rental contract must include

blocks.text: These are the blocks that can't be missing. The downloadable template already has them all; here's why each one matters.

items: Party details: rental company (legal name, tax ID, address) and renter (name, ID or passport, phone).
Craft identification: make, model, registration or hull number and power.
Rental period: date, handover time and agreed return time.
Price, payment method and deposit: amount, method and refund conditions.
Craft condition: description of prior damage and fuel level at handover.
Insurance and coverage: what the policy covers and what excess or damage the customer assumes.
Conditions of use: permitted navigation area, minimum distance from shore and prohibitions (alcohol, number of occupants, etc.).
Liability: the renter is responsible for damage, administrative penalties and third parties during the rental.
Data protection: legal basis and purpose of processing, with reference to the GDPR.
Signature of both parties and date.

hero.h1: Jet ski rental regulations in Spain
hero.lede: What you need to rent jet skis legally in Spain: licensing, insurance, Harbour Master authorizations, navigation zones and mandatory documentation. In a clear guide for operators starting out or getting compliant.

normativa.disclaimer: This guide is for guidance only and does not constitute legal advice. Nautical regulations depend on national, regional and local rules, and on each area's Harbour Master (Capitanía Marítima). Always confirm the current requirements with your Harbour Master and an advisor before operating.

sections.h: What you need to rent jet skis legally

blocks.text: In Spain, jet ski rental (jet skis are considered recreational craft) is regulated by the Directorate-General of the Merchant Marine and supervised by the Harbour Masters, on top of coastal regulations and each region's rules. As an operator you must meet requirements on four fronts: the rider's license, insurance, activity authorizations and documentation.

items: Craft (jet skis) properly registered and with their inspections up to date.
Mandatory civil-liability insurance for each craft.
Authorization to run the activity and, depending on the area, occupation of public domain.
Valid license or authorization for whoever operates the craft.
Logbook and documentation for each rental.

sections.h: Licensing: does the customer need one?

blocks.text: It depends on the craft's power and the rental format. Broadly there are three paths:

items: Navigation license: allows operating limited-power jet skis after a short theory-and-practice course. The usual route for customers who want to ride on their own.
Higher nautical qualification (PNB, PER…): for more powerful craft a higher qualification is required depending on the craft's category.
Guided or 'baptism' format: the customer rides without a license inside a marked circuit under the direct supervision of a qualified instructor. The most common format for tourist rentals.

blocks.text: The classification of craft by power and the qualification required can change; confirm with your Harbour Master which category applies to each model in your fleet.
Beyond the customer, the rental company must be compliant to offer the service.

items: Registration of the economic activity and the corresponding tax compliance.
Authorization for the rental activity and, if you operate from a beach or maritime-terrestrial public domain, the concession or occupation authorization.
Craft registered in the company's name, with technical inspection in force where applicable.
Safety and rescue means required for the activity.
Instructors with the appropriate qualification for the guided format.

blocks.text: Each jet ski must have mandatory civil-liability insurance covering damage to third parties. For your business it's also wise to have broader coverage.

items: Mandatory civil liability per craft (damage to third parties).
Own-damage coverage for the craft, with its excess.
Coverage for the activity and instructors in the guided format.

blocks.text: Renting a craft without mandatory insurance in force is a serious offense and, after an accident, can leave you exposed to respond with your own assets.

sections.h: Navigation zones and distance from shore

blocks.text: Jet skis can't navigate just anywhere. Their use is restricted to protect bathers and the coastline.

items: Departure and return only through the channels or marked zones set up for it.
No navigating inside bathing areas or closer than the minimum distance from shore set by local rules.
Respect for speed and safety distances to bathers, divers and other vessels.
Daytime navigation and within the limits of the authorization.

blocks.text: Each rental generates paperwork you must be able to show in an inspection: the customer contract, the safety-briefing statement and the activity logbook.
Keeping this up to date in peak season is where most operators slip, and where it's easiest for a detail to be missing in an inspection.

Breaches of navigation and maritime-safety rules can mean significant fines and, in serious cases, immobilization of the craft or loss of the authorization. Navigating out of zone, without insurance or without the proper license are among the most penalized.
Because the craft are registered to your company, many penalties arrive in your name even when the offender is the customer. That's why the contract must explicitly transfer that liability.

faq.q: Does the customer need a license to rent a jet ski?
faq.a: It depends on the craft's power and the format. To ride solo you usually need at least a navigation license; for powerful craft, a higher qualification. In the guided or 'baptism' format, the customer can ride without a license inside a marked, supervised circuit.

faq.q: What insurance is mandatory to rent jet skis?
faq.a: Each craft must have mandatory civil-liability insurance covering damage to third parties. For the business, adding own-damage and activity coverage is recommended.

faq.q: Where can jet skis navigate?
faq.a: They can only enter and exit through the authorized channels or marked zones, can't navigate inside bathing areas and must respect the minimum distance from shore and bathers set by local rules. Confirm the exact limits with your Harbour Master.

faq.q: What if a customer commits an offense with my craft?
faq.a: Because the craft is registered to your company, many penalties can arrive in your name. A contract that explicitly transfers liability for damage and fines to the renter is key to passing them on.

faq.a: Yes, the activity requires documenting rentals. See how in our guide on the jet ski logbook.

libro.disclaimer: This guide is for guidance only and does not constitute legal advice. Logbook requirements may vary by Harbour Master and regional rules. Confirm the format and required data with your Harbour Master.

blocks.text: The logbook is the document where the operator records every use of its jet skis: who rented it, when it left and returned, with which craft and under what conditions. It works as your fleet's activity history and is what shows, in an inspection, that you operate in an orderly and traceable way.
It can be kept on paper (one notebook per base) or digitally. What matters is that it's complete, up to date and available when requested.

The rental activity requires keeping documentation and traceability of each operation, and Harbour Masters can require the activity record in an inspection. Although the exact format can vary by area, keeping an orderly logbook is an expected practice and protects you against claims or incidents.
Check with your Harbour Master whether a specific format or a stamped book is required; in some areas the requirement is stricter than in others.

sections.h: What data each entry must contain

blocks.text: Each line of the logbook should let you reconstruct a complete rental. At a minimum:

items: Date and time of departure and return.
Craft identification (registration or hull number).
Details of the customer who rented it (name and ID).
License or format (own license, guided or baptism).
Responsible instructor, if applicable.
Incidents: breakdowns, delays, damage or penalties.
Confirmation that safety equipment was handed over (life jacket, etc.).

sections.h: How to keep the logbook, step by step

items: Before each departure, record the craft, the customer and the departure time.
Record the customer's license or the format (guided or baptism) and the assigned instructor.
Confirm and note the handover of the life jacket and safety gear.
On return, record the return time and any incident (damage, delay, penalty).
Close the entry and file it so you can retrieve it by date, craft or customer.
Periodically check that no data is missing: an incomplete entry is as good as none.

sections.h: Common mistakes that work against you

blocks.text: The most common mistake is filling it in 'later': at the end of the day, from memory. In peak season gaps pile up and, when the inspection or claim arrives, exactly the data for the problem rental is missing.

items: Incomplete or illegible entries.
A single notebook that gets wet, lost or left at another base.
Not recording the format or instructor for baptisms.
No record that safety equipment was handed over.
